statements.quote: Two hundred individuals volunteered for this 15-person trial. If we conduct ourselves ethically, these studies will continue to enroll robustly.
statements.context: Two hundred people volunteered for the 15-person veteran psilocybin trial. The author predicts veteran psychedelic studies will keep enrolling strongly if researchers conduct themselves ethically.

statements.finder_note: Conditional ('If we conduct ourselves ethically').

statements.quote: More transparency would put this kind of speculation to rest, but that's not what we've gotten from that sizeable corporate entity, and I doubt we will.

The author expects no more transparency from the company.

statements.finder_note: Negative call: the author does not expect UnitedHealthcare to become transparent about layoffs or offshore staffing.

statements.quote: Our editorial point of view is that medical devices that modulate the brain will be the future.
statements.context: Review of the Nature Medicine phase 2 fully remote sham-controlled trial of home-based transcranial direct current stimulation (Flow Neuroscience device; the author nicknames it HEAD-TRIP, real name EMPOWER). Opening editorial stance: brain-modulating medical devices, not oral medicines, will be the future of treatment.
statements.post_title: The Devices Are Coming! Depression Treated At-Home Without Meds?
statements.finder_note: Restates a recurring editorial thesis of the newsletter; contrasted with Elon Musk's 'it's coming' self-driving promises.

statements.quote: Despite being an at-home trial, it probably doesn't generalize to Medicaid populations easily, for example.
statements.context: Same tDCS review; after listing the trial's exclusion criteria (no prior ketamine or esketamine, no psychiatric hospitalization, no bipolar, PTSD, OCD or primary anxiety diagnoses, a current psychiatrist and an up-to-date phone required), the author judges the results unlikely to generalize to Medicaid populations.
statements.post_title: The Devices Are Coming! Depression Treated At-Home Without Meds?
statements.finder_note: Borderline: generalizability judgment about the EMPOWER trial; implicitly a call about results in broader, sicker populations.

statements.quote: And we shouldn't expect that from tDCS, based on prior studies.
statements.context: Same review; the author asks whether home tDCS is 'at home SAINT TMS' and answers no: tDCS should not be expected to match SAINT-level efficacy, based on prior studies (pooled tDCS effect size 0.46; this trial 0.37).
statements.post_title: The Devices Are Coming! Depression Treated At-Home Without Meds?
statements.finder_note: Negative expectation: tDCS will not reach SAINT-like effect sizes.

statements.quote: I think that will take technology and better contracts

statements.finder_note: Vague structural claim about what improvement in mental health care will require.

statements.quote: This is why expensive and error-prone universal screening like preneuvo is a terrible idea. The test will get it wrong enough that people will be subjected to subsequent risk from excessive and invasive workups to follow up on an incidental finding that wouldn't have mattered.

statements.finder_note: General predictive claim about the consequences of universal screening; a recurring position of the author.

statements.post_title: Cobenfy
statements.finder_note: Post-marketing safety call; question-and-answer form.

statements.quote: RCTs aren’t going away any time soon—they’re still an important tool. But like SSRIs, they can’t be the solution that we rely on as gold standard
statements.context: Closing thesis of Ben Spielberg's guest essay: randomized controlled trials will remain in use but should not be the sole gold standard. The author closes the post with 'Thanks, Ben, for sharing this with us, I tend to agree.'

statements.finder_note: Guest text endorsed by the author ('I tend to agree'), so own_claim set true; second sentence is normative, first is predictive.

statements.quote: We have written about the potential for GLP-1 medicines (Brand names Ozempic, Monjauro, Wegovy, Zepbound, etc.) to reduce, among other things, my personal problems of diabetes and obesity and, maybe, help with addiction.

statements.finder_note: Borderline; restatement of an earlier hedged call. The author spells Mounjaro as 'Monjauro'.

statements.quote: Alcohol use disorder has been difficult to treat, but it may be that semeglutide, liraglutide, hold promise as both safer and more effective treatments in subsequent evaluations.
statements.context: Conclusion of the same article. The author expects later evaluations to support GLP-1s as safer and more effective AUD treatments.
statements.post_title: GLP-1s May Work Better In Alcohol Use Disorder than Approved Treatments
statements.confidence_phrase: it may be that ... hold promise
statements.finder_note: Hedged compound call: safer and more effective than approved AUD medications.
